stakeholders.name: frontier_ai_developers
stakeholders.situation: Build and deploy frontier AI systems and set de facto governance through release practices, voluntary commitments, and funded policy advocacy. They define what counts as responsible conduct in the absence of binding rules, and they collect the largest share of the regime's gains: avoided compliance cost, accelerated iteration speed, and compounding capability and market advantage. Exit is easy in principle — entities can incorporate across jurisdictions, serve markets selectively, and relocate compute — which disciplines any single government considering binding rules.

stakeholders.name: venture_capital_investors
stakeholders.situation: Finance the capability race on fund-cycle timescales. Returns depend on rapid deployment and minimal compliance drag, so they fund accelerationist policy advocacy and treat regulatory proposals as portfolio risk. Capital is mobile across sectors and borders; they bear almost none of the regime's displacement or access costs.

stakeholders.name: early_adopter_professionals
stakeholders.situation: Capture the productivity and augmentation gains the reading promises — coding assistance, diagnostic support, financial tooling — while bearing little of the adjustment burden falling on displaced occupations. They can retrain, switch employers, and adopt new tools as they ship. Their lived evidence that augmentation enhances capability anchors the reading's public plausibility.

stakeholders.name: automation_displaced_workers
stakeholders.situation: Bear the displacement, wage-pressure, and job-quality costs of automation deployed under minimal-adjustment policy. Retraining programs are thin relative to the pace of substitution, mortgage and care obligations pin them to regions and occupations, and they have no formal seat in AI governance design. Their costs are the externalized half of the regime's ledger.

stakeholders.name: digital_divide_communities
stakeholders.situation: Lack the broadband, devices, capital, and skills needed to reach the enhancement side of the ledger, while services increasingly migrate into AI-mediated channels they cannot navigate. As capability concentrates, exclusion compounds across generations. They are absent from the consultations that shape the regime and cannot vote with adoption they cannot afford.

stakeholders.name: ai_safety_ethicists
stakeholders.situation: Raise alignment, concentration, and societal-harm concerns inside laboratories and academic forums. Their findings are routinely reframed as friction, PR risk, or competitive disadvantage, and their career paths run through the very institutions whose incentives they would constrain — criticizing funder and employer collapses the platform the critique depends on. Leaving removes them from the conversation entirely, so most stay and soften.

stakeholders.name: competition_and_sector_regulators
stakeholders.situation: Hold formal oversight mandates over AI deployment but operate with thin statutory authority, small technical staffs, and consultation channels dominated by regulated firms. Remedies arrive case-by-case and after deployment. They take testimony, commission analysis, and can alter enforcement conditions, but the standing arrangement treats their activity as friction to be minimized.

six_questions.coordination_function: Solves a real coordination problem: beneficial AI development — medical diagnostics, scientific acceleration, productivity tooling — requires freedom to experiment, deploy, and iterate quickly, and heavy precautionary licensing could plausibly delay capability gains the reading counts as dignity-serving. The regime coordinates capital, talent, and compute toward rapid capability expansion under a shared presumption that innovation is beneficial.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves decision-making authority over AI deployment from public and regulatory bodies to private firms and markets; moves adjustment costs (displacement, skill obsolescence, access exclusion) onto workers and unconnected communities; moves capability gains, returns, and avoided compliance cost to developers, investors, and early adopters.
six_questions.absent_voices: Automation-displaced workers and digitally excluded communities hold no formal seat in AI governance design; safety and ethics researchers inside labs face platform-dependent marginalization; religious and dignity-as-gift traditions are framed in advance as anti-science friction. The unanimity of pro-innovation consensus is partly manufactured by who was never admitted to the room.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If the minimal-restriction stance vanished overnight, binding licensing and deployment rules would expand across jurisdictions, capital would repricing AI portfolios against compliance risk, deployment pace would slow in regulated sectors, and the governance conversation would reorganize around the sibling readings' mechanisms — doctrinal, rights-based, or negotiated frameworks — rather than around market discipline.
six_questions.founding_problem: The arrangement was built to prevent precautionary governance from foreclosing capability expansion: the founding worry was that licensing regimes, liability exposure, and treaty-style controls built before AI matured would strangle cures, abundance, and scientific acceleration that would ultimately serve human dignity.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: Proponents — laboratory leadership, investor coalitions, accelerationist policy shops — attest liveness, citing regulatory-delay cases. Outside corroboration is partial and split: mainstream economists acknowledge a real innovation-value tradeoff, but labor organizations, patient-safety advocates, and international governance bodies attest that the operative problem has shifted to unchecked deployment harms, and no fully independent body attests the founding problem in its original precautionary-foreclosure form.

commentary.narrative_context: This file instantiates ONE reading of the contested human_dignity_ai_governance kernel: the techno-optimist reading, under which human dignity is enhanced through technological augmentation, AI is a tool for transcending biological limits, and governance should minimize restrictions. The standing arrangement under contest — and the epsilon referent — is the light-touch AI governance regime as it actually operates in leading AI jurisdictions: voluntary frameworks instead of binding licensing, sectoral patchwork instead of horizontal statute, market discipline and reputational enforcement doing the work doctrine, law, or negotiation would do under the sibling readings. Assessed by this reading's own lights the regime is liberating; assessed descriptively it concentrates capability and returns while externalizing displacement and access costs. The claimed type and the metrics are authored independently: the reading CLAIMS a coordination-first regime (its own self-description is closer to rope), while the metrics describe substantially extractive operation — the engine measures that divergence rather than either reconciling them or trusting the claim. Family membership: the colloquial label 'AI governance and human dignity' decomposes into four structurally distinct readings with distinct epsilon, victim sets, and enforcement modes; the siblings (magisterial-integralist, secular-humanist, pluralist-pragmatic) are separate constraint files linked through network.affects_constraints, per DP-001 epsilon-invariance.
key_agents: - frontier_ai_developers: Agenda setter ([institutional]/[arbitrage]) — sets de facto governance via deployment norms, voluntary commitments, and funded policy advocacy; collects the largest share of the regime's gains
- venture_capital_investors: Primary beneficiary ([powerful]/[arbitrage]) — finances the capability race; bears none of its externalized costs
- early_adopter_professionals: Secondary beneficiary ([moderate]/[mobile]) — captures augmentation gains; anchors the reading's public plausibility
- automation_displaced_workers: Primary target ([powerless]/[trapped]) — bears displacement and wage-pressure costs with no governance seat
- digital_divide_communities: Secondary target ([powerless]/[trapped]) — bears compounding access-exclusion costs across generations
- ai_safety_ethicists: Excluded critic ([moderate]/[identity_locked]) — raises harm concerns; platform-dependent, reframed as friction
- competition_and_sector_regulators: Analytical observer ([institutional]/[analytical]) — holds oversight mandates the standing arrangement treats as friction
commentary.logic_rationale: Extraction is high (0.73 at interval end) because the regime's gains — avoided compliance cost, deployment speed, compounding capability advantage — concentrate at the developer seat while displacement and access costs fall on seats with no exit and no voice. Suppression (0.65, raw and unscaled per the framework rule; only extractiveness is scaled by directionality and scope) reflects the machinery that holds regulatory alternatives open to challenge: lobbying capacity, consultation-channel dominance, forum control, and the framing of regulation-as-friction. Theater ratio (0.44 and rising) tracks the substitution of voluntary pledges, ethics boards without binding authority, and safety institutes without enforcement power for the rules they resemble — functional activity remains (real capability delivery, real research) but a growing share of governance-shaped activity is performative compliance-substitute. Accessibility collapse is moderate (0.55): the minimal-restriction frame forecloses much regulatory imagination ('any rule is friction'), yet the sibling readings remain live in discourse and in other files, so alternatives are narrowed rather than eliminated. Resistance is substantial (0.62): labor organizing, EU-style binding legislation, religious-body objection, and internal safety advocacy all contest the frame. The measurement series run on ONE shared grid (t=0..14, roughly 2012-2026) with all three metrics authored at every point. The trajectories are ratchets, not cycles: extractiveness accumulates as displacement outruns adjustment, theater grows as voluntary substitutes accrete, and suppression_requirement is authored deliberately because the enforcement picture is dynamic — the defensive infrastructure (lobbying spend, capture networks, voluntary-standard apparatus) visibly built out over the interval. Suppression mechanism split: approximately 70% structural (resource asymmetry, capture, forum control) and 30% internalized (policymakers' learned belief that regulation is futile), routed to the dedicated omega.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The payer and excluded seats and the agenda-setter seat should compute sharply differently. From the developer and investor positions the arrangement is a coordination achievement they built, fund, and defend: freedom to build is experienced as the whole substance of the constraint, and per-seat classification from those seats trends rope-like or benign. From the trapped payer seats the identical structure operates as enforced extraction — the same voluntariness that reads as liberty at the center reads as the absence of protection at the edges. The identity-locked excluded seat (safety ethicists) experiences a third mode: constraint as silencing — participation permitted, effect denied. The engine computes this divergence from power, exit, and role data; the authored claim adjudicates nothing.
commentary.directionality_logic: Directionality follows the declared structure. Frontier developers derive d near the beneficiary pole: they author the arrangement and sit at arbitrage-grade exit, so effective extraction inverts toward subsidy. Venture investors and early adopters derive low d as beneficiaries with mobile or arbitrage exit. Automation-displaced workers and digital-divide communities derive d near the full-target pole: they bear the transfer with trapped exit and powerless power, and their large spatial dispersion amplifies effective extraction through the scope modifier (harder verification at larger scope). Receipt surface: gain_flow names frontier_ai_developers rather than 'diffuse' because the gains demonstrably accrue to that seat — capability lead, revenue share, and the entire avoided-compliance margin land there; calling the receipt diffuse would falsely assert no capturer exists. fixing_cost is authored 'prohibitive': for any single government, imposing binding rules triggers capital flight and jurisdiction arbitrage (the developer seat's defining exit), so the cost to the unilateral fixer exceeds the benefit it captures; only coordinated multilateral action changes the calculus, and no such coordinator currently exists. Coalition check: the payer seats are individually powerless but coalition-capable — labor federations, consumer advocates, and cross-jurisdictional regulatory alliances are the identified path by which trapped targets convert diffuse cost into organized countervailing power; the resistance metric partially registers this and would rise sharply under successful coalition formation.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding mandate — keep precautionary governance from foreclosing capability expansion — is contested rather than dead: proponents attest liveness, outside corroborators largely attest the operative problem has shifted to unchecked harms. The classification guards against mislabeling in both directions. Reading the regime as pure snare erases its genuine coordination component (rapid beneficial deployment is real, and some freedom-to-operate is a real precondition for it); reading it as pure rope erases the asymmetric extraction (same structure coordinates the center and extracts at the edges, held in place by actively maintained enforcement). Tangled rope is the structurally honest claim. The decay vector runs toward piton-and-snare territory: theater_ratio above 0.5 would signal the voluntary-apparatus replacing function entirely, and if enhancement access stays concentrated while costs continue to socialize, the remaining coordination story thins into rent defense. mandatrophy_resolved is NOT flagged: the mandate has not plainly outlived its function, but the mismatch consumer should watch founding_problem_status=contested against the computed theater trajectory.
commentary.kernel_context: Kernel: human_dignity_ai_governance — the contested question of what AI governance owes to human dignity. This file instantiates the techno_optimist_reading: dignity as enhanced through technological augmentation, governance minimized to protect innovation and individual choice. Sibling readings, each a separate constraint file: magisterial_integralist_reading (dignity as infinite ontological gift, governance conformed to Magisterial doctrine), secular_humanist_reading (dignity as rational autonomy and equal moral status, governance by democratic deliberation and law), pluralist_pragmatic_reading (dignity as culturally contested, governance by negotiated overlap and procedural fairness). The structural disagreement is located primarily in the ONTOLOGY of dignity (augmentable quantity vs. fixed divine gift vs. equal autonomous status vs. contested concept) and secondarily in the enforcement mechanism (market/voluntary vs. doctrinal vs. legal-democratic vs. negotiated-procedural). This reading's relations: it forecloses the integralist sibling (an augmentable dignity and an infinite inalienable one cannot coexist in one framework), coexists with the secular-humanist sibling (both remain live positions across factions; the techno-optimist reading even borrows the sibling's autonomy vocabulary while bypassing its democratic mechanism), and exerts downstream influence on the pluralist sibling (resource asymmetry tilts any negotiated framework without logically eliminating it).

network.dual_formulation_note: Constraint-family decomposition of the kernel human_dignity_ai_governance. The colloquial label 'AI governance consistent with human dignity' conflates four structurally distinct claims with different epsilon values, victim sets, and enforcement modes; per DP-001 they are modeled as four linked stories rather than one story with a measurement parameter. Upstream/downstream structure: the secular_humanist_reading is the established liberal-rights baseline (UDHR-lineage, highest empirical confidence) whose autonomy and individual-choice vocabulary the techno-optimist reading cites rhetorically while bypassing its democratic-deliberation mechanism — the upstream sibling legitimizes the downstream reading's language without its governance commitments. The magisterial_integralist_reading supplies the theological counter-frame against which the techno-optimist reading defines its secularized dignity-as-capability claim. Every member of this family links to the others through network.affects_constraints.

omegas.question: How would each sibling reading of the human_dignity_ai_governance kernel change the structural content of this constraint?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Cross-reading comparison within the kernel family: instantiate the sibling stories (magisterial-integralist, secular-humanist, pluralist-pragmatic) and compare their victim sets, enforcement modes, and epsilon values against this file's.
omegas.impact: Sibling readings relocate the victim set (integralist: dignity violated as commodification of the person; secular-humanist: rights violated by governance outside democratic deliberation; pluralist: persons violated by procedural exclusion) and swap enforcement from market/voluntary to doctrinal, legal, or procedural mechanisms. This story's classification stands on its own structural data regardless; the omega records that it is one reading of a kernel, naming the reading, and that the disagreement is located in dignity's ontology and the enforcement mechanism.
omegas.description: Committer structure: this constraint is one reading (techno-optimist) of the human_dignity_ai_governance kernel; siblings are separate constraints.

omegas.question: Is the structural disagreement among the sibling readings located in the definition of dignity itself (augmentable vs. gifted vs. autonomous-equal vs. contested) or only in the governance mechanism (market vs. doctrine vs. law vs. negotiation)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Analytical decomposition of each reading's axioms: test whether readings sharing a dignity definition but differing on mechanism produce divergent classifications, and whether readings sharing a mechanism but differing on dignity converge.
omegas.impact: If disagreement sits in dignity's ontology, the techno-optimist/integralist pair is genuinely mutually foreclosing and foreclosure computations fire; if it sits only in mechanism, all pairs reduce to coexistence and the reading_relations graph simplifies to influence edges.
omegas.description: Where in the kernel the readings' structural disagreement is actually located.

omegas.question: Is this reading's dignity claim conditional on broad access to augmentation, and does the classification change if enhancement capability remains concentrated among resourced adopters?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Longitudinal access data: diffusion rates of productivity-enhancing AI tools across income strata, regions, and firm sizes over the interval.
omegas.impact: If access stays concentrated while costs continue to socialize, the coordination story loses its dignity-for-all warrant and effective extraction climbs toward snare territory; broad access would vindicate the rope-side reading and dampen measured extraction.
omegas.description: Whether dignity-through-augmentation survives as a coordination claim under concentrated access.

omegas.question: Is rapid beneficial capability development genuinely better coordinated under minimal restriction than under binding-but-light regulation, or is the coordination claim cover for compliance-cost avoidance?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Natural experiment comparing beneficial-deployment rates (medical, scientific, productivity) in jurisdictions with binding AI statutes against minimal-rule regimes, controlling for sector and scale.
omegas.impact: If beneficial deployment continues under binding rules, the measured suppression of regulation is extraction-enforcing rather than coordination-preserving and the tangled-rope balance tips toward snare; if deployment stalls under rules, part of the measured extraction is the genuine price of the coordination itself.
omegas.description: Whether the regime's coordination and extraction components are structurally separable.

omegas.question: Are the automation-displacement costs borne by the payer seats structurally internalizable through policy (retraining, transfers, portability), or inherent to the acceleration the reading prescribes?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative analysis of jurisdictions pairing rapid AI adoption with robust adjustment policy against those adopting rapidly without it.
omegas.impact: If costs are internalizable, the victims are policy-addressable and the constraint reads as incomplete coordination awaiting repair; if inherent, the externalization is structural and the extraction assessment hardens permanently.
omegas.description: Scope of the externalization: addressable policy residue or structural feature of acceleration.

omegas.question: Is the suppression of regulatory alternatives structural (lobbying capacity, capture networks, forum control) or internalized (policymakers' learned belief that regulation is futile)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Post-capture suppression trajectory: if regulatory timidity persists in jurisdictions after lobbying capacity is removed (post-disclosure or post-scandal), reclassify the residual as partially internalized.
omegas.impact: Internalized suppression outlasts its structural basis, raising effective persistence beyond what lobbying disclosures suggest; structural suppression responds to transparency and counter-lobbying. Current estimate: roughly 70% structural, 30% internalized.
omegas.description: Structural vs. internalized mechanism of the regime's suppression of regulatory alternatives.
